title: Google Pixel Watch 5 Leaks Reveal New Colors, Price Hike Ahead of August Launch
excerpt: Official press renders show four colorways matching the Pixel 11 lineup, while reports point to the first price increase in the smartwatch’s four-year history.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Google Pixel Watch 5 leaks reveal four new colors matching the Pixel 11 lineup.
  • The 41mm Wi-Fi model will start at $399, a $50 price increase.
  • Launch event scheduled for August 12, with a release date of August 20.
  • Processor choice remains uncertain between Qualcomm Snapdragon and Google Tensor.
  • The watch will support NFC, GPS, and ultra-wideband for improved connectivity.

The Google Pixel Watch 5 has surfaced in official press renders just weeks before its expected unveiling, showing a familiar design in four new colorways alongside reports of the first price increase the smartwatch line has seen since its 2022 debut.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=WgUASVGX-m8

The leaked renders, first reported by Android Headlines and corroborated by multiple outlets, show Dark Anthracite, Natural Silver, Pyrite, and Warm Gold finishes — each chosen to complement the corresponding color options for the upcoming Pixel 11 smartphone range. The design carries over largely unchanged from the Pixel Watch 4, consistent with Google’s pattern of concentrating improvements on internal hardware and software.

First Price Increase in Four Years

Multiple leaks indicate that Google is raising prices across the Pixel Watch lineup for the first time. The 41mm Wi-Fi model is expected to start at $399, up from $349 for the Pixel Watch 4 — a 14 percent increase. The 45mm LTE variant could climb to $529, according to reports from 9to5Google and other outlets.

European pricing is also expected to rise, with the 41mm Wi-Fi model reportedly starting at €419 and the 45mm LTE version reaching €549. Industry analysts have attributed the increases to rising component costs tied to the global RAM shortage and potentially more expensive chipsets.

Processor Remains the Biggest Question

The most significant unknown heading into the August launch is which processor the Pixel Watch 5 will use. Reports are divided. Some point to Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon Wear Elite chipset as the likely choice, while others — including leaked documents reported by Android Authority earlier this year — suggest Google may switch to its own Tensor silicon, mirroring the strategy it has used with Pixel smartphones.

A custom Tensor chip built on TSMC’s 3nm node with Cortex-A78 and A55 CPU cores would represent a significant leap in performance and efficiency. More importantly, it would enable on-device AI processing, allowing features like health insights and workout analysis without a network connection — and with greater data privacy.

“Between RAMageddon and Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon Wear Elite chipset — the latter not confirmed, but heavily implied — Google’s material costs have most definitely gone up this year.”

— 9to5Google

What Else to Expect

The Pixel Watch 5 will ship in 41mm and 45mm cases with Wi-Fi and LTE options. Certification listings have confirmed NFC, GPS, and ultra-wideband (UWB) support, which enables more precise device tracking and improved connectivity with other Pixel devices. The watch is expected to run Wear OS 7 and feature tighter Gemini AI integration, with leaked renders showing a dedicated Gemini shortcut on a redesigned watch face.

One area where the watch will not improve is charging. Google will continue using the proprietary pin-based charging system introduced with the Pixel Watch 4, passing on the opportunity to adopt the universal Qi2 wireless standard that would allow third-party chargers and reduce accessory costs. The official charging dock costs $30, with limited third-party alternatives available.

August 12 Unveiling

Google has confirmed a Made by Google event on August 12 to launch its new Pixel devices, with the Pixel Watch 5 expected alongside the Pixel 11 series. A reported August 20 release date would put it in stores just over a week later. With Apple and Samsung both expected to refresh their wearable lineups this year, Google’s pricing and performance improvements will face immediate scrutiny from competitors offering established ecosystems and broader accessory support.
